saying “it has unique human dna” literally proves nothing ethically lol it’s not even useful for defining what a human being is. in science and bioethics we talk about necessary and sufficient characteristics. necessary = it HAS to be there. sufficient = if it’s there, that alone is enough. unique human dna is neither bro it’s not sufficient, cuz if it was then wed have to consider certain tumors as persons (teratomas have unique dna yet no one argues we’re committing murder when we remove them). and b4 anyone goes “omg how r u comparing a fetus to a tumor”, i’m not. i’m js explaining why dna alone doesn’t magically make something a person, but whatever u wanna hear ig.
it’s also not necessary. identical twins exist and they come from the same embryo and have the same dna yet no legal system on earth considers them one person or no person at all lmao there’s also chimerism, where one individual can have two different sets of dna. so if dna was the defining factor, these cases would completely break the concept of personhood but they don’t and guess why CUZ DNA WAS NEVER THE POINT.
and here’s the thing ppl love to ignore and answers ur question: there is NO strict scientific consensus on when someone becomes a “human being” in the moral or legal sense. biology can describe processes, not assign personhood. that’s why what we use in practice are operational definitions, theyre practical definitions that let us legislate and make medical decisions while minimizing harm, a good example is temperature since it used to be defined as “whatever a thermometer measures” before physics fully explained it, personhood is defined operationally in law and medicine. and guess what those definitions focus on? not dna but brain activity and neurological function
that’s why someone who is brain dead is legally dead EVEN THO their cells are still alive, reproducing, and carrying human dna. we don’t keep brain dead bodies alive just to preserve genetic material, and we don’t ban organ donation over that either since it would be dumb to not save someone else's life js to preserve a body that's not even a subject of rights (sounds familiar huh?) if human dna was enough, none of this

As a Kantian ethicist, I really can do nothing but wholeheartedly reject this idea lol. The existence of a body, even a living one, does not entitle something to moral value. And it happening to be a human body does not magically grant that moral value either. Where value truly can be said to derive from is the mind, the capacity for an independent, subjective experience. A fetus doesn’t possess that and is incapable of possessing it, not until around week 26 at the absolute earliest and week 35-ish at the very latest. If it’s true that the mind gives life its value, which I believe it does as value and meaning in and of itself derives from the mind and thus seems to be the only reasonable measure that balances human dignity with bodily autonomy and provides a coherent model for understanding the source of moral value, then we can’t in good conscience condemn the killing of a fetus for the vast majority of the gestation period any more than we can condemn the picking of flowers or the mowing of grass
